rounds.text: Capri Global Capital Ltd is displaying extraordinary operational momentum, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of 45% over 5 years and an astonishing 53% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. This top-line expansion translates directly to the bottom line, with profit growth accelerating by 83% over the trailing twelve months and a rules-based screen scoring the business a strong 85 out of 100 for a buy [E21, E61]. The company's profitability metrics comfortably outshine sector benchmarks, highlighted by an ROA of 3.27% compared to the sector average of 1.93% and an ROE of 16.46% versus 5.27% [E8, E9]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is surging, as foreign institutions have increased their holdings by 12.19 percentage points since December 2023, driving positive institutional money flow [E37, E39]. Valuation models also suggest significant unrealised upside, with a reverse DCF indicating that the current market price of ₹ 245 prices in a mere 6.8% earnings growth against a base-case assumption of 18.0% [E2, E42]. Conceded: [E30], [E31], [E32].

Capri Global Capital Ltd carries severe fundamental risks that are entirely obscured by headline growth figures. Most critically, the company's operating cash flow and free cash flow for March 2026 have collapsed to massive negative figures of Rs -8,728 Cr and Rs -8,786 Cr respectively, resulting in an alarming cash conversion ratio of -9.20x [E30, E31, E32]. This severe liquidity drain is compounded by a precarious balance sheet structure where current liabilities exceed current assets, yielding a current ratio of 0.88x, alongside a high debt-to-equity ratio of 3.09x where non-current liabilities exceed equity capital [E33, E34]. Furthermore, the business suffers from a low interest coverage ratio and a low three-year median return on equity of 12.6% [E58, E59]. Insider behavior and historical volatility also present formidable concerns for investors. Promoters have steadily abandoned their stake, reducing holdings by nearly 10 percentage points from 69.88% in December 2023 to 59.92% by September 2026 [E36, E60]. Compounding this insider retreat, the equity exhibits extreme annualised volatility of 58.1% and a devastating historical worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.2% [E48, E49]. Additionally, filed statements explicitly flag that earnings growth is decelerating [E66], and the stock trades at an elevated 2.97 times its book value [E57]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E16, E17, E18, E19, E20, E21, E37, E38, E39]

Conceded: [E30, E31, E32, E33, E34, E48, E49, E57, E58, E59, E60, E66]. Despite the liquidity and balance sheet markers cited, the business demonstrates robust operating momentum through exceptional compounded sales growth reaching 53% over the trailing twelve months and profit growth accelerating by 83% [E17, E21]. This outpaces the broader sector significantly, where median sales growth is 16.7% and profit growth is 21.5% [E69, E70]. Furthermore, institutional investors are actively endorsing this performance through positive money flow with foreign and domestic holdings expanding by 12.19 and 2.90 percentage points respectively [E37, E38, E39]. The valuation remains highly attractive, with a rules-based screen scoring the stock 85 out of 100 as a buy [E61], a discounted cash flow intrinsic value well above the market price providing a 55.8% margin of safety [E40, E41], and a reverse DCF indicating that the current price merely requires a modest 6.8% earnings growth against the 18.0% base case [E42].

Conceded: [E17, E21, E37, E38, E39, E69, E70]. While those growth figures and institutional inflows exist, the underlying financial stability supporting them is severely compromised by negative operating cash flow of Rs -8,728 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -8,786 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31, E32], leading to an alarming cash conversion ratio of -9.20x [E30]. The bull leans heavily on models like the rules-based screen and DCF [E61, E40, E41, E42], yet ignores explicit fundamental warnings flagged by the company, including low interest coverage, a low return on equity of 12.6% over the last three years [E58, E59], and decelerating earnings growth [E66]. Balance sheet stress is further highlighted by a heavy debt-to-equity leverage proxy of 3.09x and a sub-one current ratio of 0.88x [E33, E34]. Furthermore, promoters continue to vote with their feet by reducing their stake by 9.99% over three years [E60], coinciding with extreme historical volatility of 58.1% and a devastating peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.2% [E48, E49].
